title: From the Lens of Stakeholder’s Management Theory: Exploring the Relationship Between Knowledge Management and Firm Performance, the Mediating Role of Corporate Social Responsibility
content: Purpose- Sustainability themes have become watchwords of contemporary enterprises. Businesses are confronted with the challenges of integrating emerging stakeholders interests into operating strategies. Successful ventures capitalize on knowledge management to incorporate stakeholders demand into market offering. The aim of the study was to investigate the relationship between Knowledge management, corporate social responsibility, and firm performance. Design/methodology approach- Empirical data was collected from 220 participants drawn from various European firms who appeared in the 100 most sustainable corporation in the world in the year 2020 global ranking. Smart PLS was utilized in data processing and testing of the study hypotheses. Findings- The results show a positive direct association between the constructs of knowledge management and corporate social responsibility, knowledge management and firm performance, and corporate social responsibility and firm performance. However, the result of the mediation analysis of firm performance through corporate social responsibility shows no significant relationship. Research limitation/implication- The study limitation is associated with the development of a simple model of latent variables, which is usually not appropriate in complex investigation of this nature, therefore, the inclusion of second order variables are recommended to provide more insights. Practical implication- This study contributes toward the effective management of stakeholders interests through the deployment of knowledge management principles. Originality- The study advocate for the extension of knowledge management practices beyond organizational boundary to allow for effective stakeholders management. Thus, stakeholder’s management theory underpinned the study.
